messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] P1: GPU pool 'gpu-prod-eu' saturated; queue depth > 10k; throttling observed. Autoscaler attempted expand but failed: 'scale blocked by max_nodes (32)'. Dashboard: https://dashboard/redwood/incidents/1987654322

alice_oncall: ack - I'm oncall, taking lead. tagging @jordan_sre and @liz_infra. any initial impact numbers? :rotating_light:

jordan_sre: seeing tail of logs - continuous-batching params collapsed after a config push ~20m ago. batch_size median dropped from ~12 to ~2, throughput down ~4x. Also prefix_cache miss rate spiked to 85%.

raj_dev: that deploy was the v1.9.3 batching config change (rolled via infra/auto). I flagged a toggle: continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=2048 -> 256; prefix_cache.ttl=0 (was 60s) to test eviction.

liz_infra: autoscaler log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-15T09:31:12Z autoscaler: request_scale up to 33 nodes
2026-03-15T09:31:13Z autoscaler: rejected: account_quota=32 (current=32)
2026-03-15T09:31:14Z autoscaler: backoff, will retry
```
We hit account quota. Region quota shows 32 hard limit for this pool.

alice_oncall: we have two simultaneous problems: scale cap (can't add GPUs) + batch/caching regression reducing per-node throughput => queue skyrockets. Immediate mitigations?

emi_product: customers with active live sessions: RetailAI-prod, ChatAssist-inc, SalesQ. Product reports visible latency spikes and 5% failed requests on RetailAI. Need cust comms.

jordan_sre: suggested immediate steps: 1) rollback batching config to previous commit, 2) flush prefix cache, 3) open temporary fallback to cpu-backed small-model for low-priority traffic, 4) request quota increase (but that's slow).

raj_dev: I can roll back the batching/prefixcache change now. Pushing revert in 2m. Will annotate deploy.

deploy-bot: deploy started by raj_dev: revert-batchcfg-1987654322 (sha: a1b2c3). CI: all green.

raj_dev: revert applied. continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=2048 restored; prefix_cache.ttl=60 restored.

jordan_sre: flushing prefix cache across pool: `./tools/prefix_cache_flush --pool=gpu-prod-eu --parallel=8` - started. Expect hit-rate recovery in ~30-60s after flush.

liz_infra: temp mitigation for capacity: enabling fallback routing to other regions with spare capacity and circuit-break low-priority requests. Adjusting routing policy to offload non-critical traffic to 'gpu-prod-us' and 'gpu-staging'.

alice_oncall: who can open quota request with cloud team? This looks like hitting provider account limit.

liz_infra: opened cloud ticket INC-3421, requested +8 GPUs for eu region (sent priority). ETA unknown. Also bumped local per-customer concurrency limit to reduce queue pressure.

jordan_sre: post-rollback metrics: batch_size median climbing back to ~10 within 45s; prefix_cache hit-rate back to ~75%. Throughput improving per-node ~3.7x. Queue depth falling but still >2k.

emi_product: started customer comms draft for RetailAI-prod and SalesQ. Notifying TA teams and assigning ROs to customers above SLA thresholds.

alice_oncall: do we need to trigger failover for any VIP traffic?

liz_infra: routing change completed for non-critical PDs. Critical customers remain on eu until quota increase or backlog cleared. We set throttling policy: new global throttle to 80 tps for non-committed tenants.

raj_dev: small note - this regression was introduced by a short-lived experiment to reduce memory footprint for edge models. I'll add a guard in the deployment pipeline so batch config can't be lowered beyond safelimits without explicit perf test.

jordan_sre: mitigation summary so far: revert batching config (done), flush prefix cache (done), route non-critical traffic away (done), reduced per-customer concurrency, opened quota increase request. Observed effect: queue decreasing, tail latency improving.

alice_oncall: severity -> P1 still until queue <500 and errors <0.5%. Assigned oncall -> alice_oncall, owner -> jordan_sre, infra -> liz_infra, dev -> raj_dev, comms -> emi_product.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: revert-batchcfg-1987654322 succeeded in 1m 12s.

jordan_sre: drilling into root cause: the experiment changed two knobs that interact badly with autoscaler heuristics. Lower batch tokens reduced per-request latency (client-facing) but massively reduced packing efficiency -> autoscaler saw sustained high queue and tried to scale but hit quota. Prefix cache TTL=0 caused cold starts for repeated prefixes, amplifying KV miss storm.

emi_product: flagged for postmortem: product impact list + cust comms. Recommend a retro with infra/dev/sre to tighten change controls for batching and cache toggles.

alice_oncall: current numbers: queue depth 420, 95p latency back to baseline, error rate 0.6% trending down. Keeping P1 until <0.5% and queue <200.

liz_infra: cloud ticket updated: provider acknowledged; expedited quota increase possible but not required now. Still keeping long-term mitigation plan: increase pool max_nodes to 48, add autoscaler circuit-breaker that prefers config-based capacity before hitting global quota.

raj_dev: created PR to add validation for continuous_batching.* changes and add a canary test to perf harness. PR: https://git/repo/pull/4212

alice_oncall: good work everyone. I will keep the thread open for final closure. Next steps: postmortem, cust follow-ups, add deploy guard. :thumbsup:

emi_product: will start cust follow-ups and draft incident email.

jordan_sre: logging incident_close ETA 60min for monitoring window.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: mitigating -> monitoring. Pager rotations suspended.

alice_oncall: closing timeline note: root cause = experimental batch/cache config removed packing headroom; contributing = region quota cap. Action items documented in #incidents-postmortems.
